# Results — Study 683 (Evening-Star)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
tall up candle, a small-body "star" gapping higher, then a tall down candle marks the top
of an uptrend; short it** — tested as a clean signed-**short** event study on a fixed
**30-name liquid US large-cap + SPY** basket. For every confirming bar we enter the next
open (one lag), hold 1 / 5 / 10 days short, and measure the signed return against the
**unconditional** basket base rate (not against zero — see the note below) and against a
coin-flip placebo. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month;
2026-07 is dropped as partial). Fingerprint `bde089f6e8ee` (quantlab `data_stamp` on the
30-name close panel) / `97e1b85d26c3` (basket sha1, `data.fingerprint`).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` — 30 long-listed liquid US large-caps + **SPY** (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** (last complete calendar month; run 2026-07-10) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (**21.5** years; **162,180** total bars, 5,406 rows/name) |
| Fingerprints | `bde089f6e8ee` (quantlab `data_stamp`, 30-name close panel) / `97e1b85d26c3` (`data.fingerprint`, sha1 of the same closes) |
| Detector | precise real-body evening star on bars (t−2, t−1, t): tall bull body, small star gapping up, tall bear body closing ≥50% back into candle t−2's body; strict-gap + prior-uptrend variants for the myth-check |
| Timing / costs | confirm at close of t; enter the **next open** (one lag); hold 1/5/10 days **short**; **5 / 10 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip) + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short over the hold |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis — and it cuts the *right* way).** The basket is
> 30 names that are *still trading* in 2026. A fixed surviving-names panel **excludes the
> firms that actually topped out and crashed and delisted** — exactly the cases an
> "evening star → crash" believer would point to. So this universe is biased **toward**
> finding a working bearish signal. It still finds none, which makes the null verdict
> strong rather than an artefact of selection.

## The certifying comparison — why Welch-vs-base, not a plain t-vs-zero

The basket carries the market's ordinary positive drift (equities go up on average), so a
naive one-sample *t* of the signed-**short** return against **zero** is contaminated: it
would flag "significance" merely from shorting into an up-trending tape, with or without
any evening star. The fair test compares the event sample against the **same basket's own
unconditional forward-return pool** (Welch *t*) — beating "just shorting blindly" is the
bar an actual pattern-based edge has to clear. Both numbers are reported below; **Welch
*t* vs the unconditional base is the decisive number for the Signal axis.**

## The headline — signed-SHORT forward return after an evening star

| horizon | n events | signed-short mean | unconditional base | hit-rate (Wilson 95%) | base hit-rate | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0, informational) | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 602 | **−0.055%** | +0.028% | 50% [46.2%, 54.1%] | 48% | **−0.53** | −1.12 | 0.842 |
| 5-day  | 602 | **−0.527%** | +0.252% | 44% [40.1%, 48.0%] | 45% | **−1.84** | −3.77 | 1.000 |
| 10-day | 600 | **−0.612%** | +0.529% | 46% [42.2%, 50.2%] | 43% | **−0.43** | −2.95 | 0.999 |

Read it carefully. The signed-short mean is **negative at every horizon** — shorting the
pattern loses — but once compared *fairly* to the basket's own unconditional drift (Welch
*t*), **no horizon clears |t| ≥ 2**: −0.53, −1.84, −0.43. The naive HAC *t* against zero
*looks* significant at 5- and 10-day (−3.77, −2.95), but that is the basket's embedded
up-drift talking, not the pattern — a short of *anything* in this tape drifts negative
against zero without any evening star involved (see the synthetic control below, which
proves this exact point on data with a **known** zero pattern-edge). Hit rates sit close
to, or even *above*, the unconditional base hit rate (46% vs 43% at 10-day) — there is no
consistent directional edge either way. The coin-flip placebo *p* is high (0.84–1.00): the
observed signed-short mean sits in the territory where the large majority of random,
undirected picks would have done at least as well.

## Cost sweep — the loss only deepens

Each event is a fresh short round trip: **5 / 10 bps one-way × 2** plus **50 bps/yr**
borrow over the hold. When the gross is already negative (or, at best, statistically
indistinguishable from the base rate), costs can only bury it further.

| horizon | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −0.055% | **−0.157%** | −0.257% |
| 5-day  | −0.527% | **−0.637%** | −0.737% |
| 10-day | −0.612% | **−0.732%** | −0.832% |

There is no horizon where the short clears zero, let alone its costs, let alone the
unconditional base. Nothing under the signal to charge costs against — a textbook
**Mirage**.

## Bonferroni across the basket — no single name carries it either

Per-ticker Welch *t* (event sample vs that ticker's **own** unconditional forward-return
pool — drift-neutral) at the 5-day horizon, for the 30 tickers with ≥ 6 events. With
**k = 30** simultaneous tests the two-sided Bonferroni bar is **|t| ≥ 3.14** (vs the usual
1.96):

| ticker | n | signed-short mean | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| MMM  | 16 | −1.396% | −2.25 |
| ORCL | 17 | −2.478% | −2.07 |
| ABT  | 24 | −1.167% | −1.99 |

**0 / 30 tickers clear the corrected bar.** Even the three most extreme names in a
30-name basket — exactly the kind of outlier a chart-reader would show you — don't survive
the multiple-testing correction. No single name is quietly carrying the whole pattern.

## Myth check #1 — the strict textbook gap

Tighten the rule to the purist's evening star (the star's body doesn't touch candle t−2's
body at all — `gap_tol_frac = 0`). If the lore hid in a "cleaner" pattern, this should be
*more* bearish. It isn't (and the events are rarer):

| horizon | n | signed-short mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 284 | −0.025% | +0.04 | −0.34 | 0.614 | −0.127% |
| 5-day  | 284 | −0.451% | −0.91 | −2.45 | 0.987 | −0.561% |
| 10-day | 283 | −0.678% | −0.50 | −2.71 | 0.990 | −0.797% |

## Myth check #2 — only stars after a genuine prior uptrend (a true reversal)

An evening star is *supposed* to reverse a rally. Restrict to stars that followed a prior
uptrend (close at t−3 above its level 10 days earlier). Still nothing — the Welch *t*
against the unconditional base gets *weaker*, not stronger:

| horizon | n | signed-short mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 318 | −0.093% | −0.98 | −1.49 | 0.879 | −0.195% |
| 5-day  | 318 | −0.261% | −0.05 | −1.37 | 0.912 | −0.371% |
| 10-day | 316 | −0.267% | +1.03 | −1.06 | 0.825 | −0.387% |

Neither the strict shape nor the reversal filter produces a certifiable bearish edge. The
pattern's predictive content is indistinguishable from the basket's own drift under every
reasonable definition.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic OHLCV panel, mild embedded up-drift (so tall-up-candle evening stars
actually occur), with a TUNABLE planted post-pattern crash; no network. The certifying
statistic is Welch *t* vs the unconditional base (the same drift-neutral comparison used
on the real tape) — a plain *t*-vs-zero is contaminated by the panel's own drift exactly
the way the real basket's is, which is itself the point of this control.

| world | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0) | placebo *p* | hit-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.26** (sd 1.25), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** | — | — | — |
| null (edge = 0, seed 683) | +1.28 | −0.04 | 0.524 | 47% |
| planted edge = +0.004/day (seed 683) | **+3.54** | +2.43 | 0.011 | 53% |
| planted edge = +0.008/day (seed 683) | **+5.73** | +4.82 | 0.000 | 61% |

The null fires in 1 of 20 independent seeds at the 2-sigma bar — in line with the ~5%
nominal false-positive rate of a two-sigma test, not a systematic bias — and a planted
crash of 0.4%/day or 0.8%/day lights the detector up cleanly (*t* = 3.5 and 5.7). The
harness *would* catch a real evening-star crash if one existed, so the real-tape's failure
to certify is a genuine **absence** of signal, not a broken detector. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The certifying, drift-neutral comparison (Welch *t* vs the
  unconditional base) never reaches **|t| ≥ 2** at any horizon (−0.53 / −1.84 / −0.43 for
  1/5/10 days). Hit rates sit at or above the unconditional base rate. The coin-flip
  placebo places the observed mean where 84–100% of random draws would have matched or
  beaten it. **0 of 30 tickers** survive a Bonferroni correction individually. Neither a
  strict textbook gap nor a genuine prior-uptrend filter rescues it. Carries an explicit
  **survivorship** caveat that tilts the test *toward* the claim — and it still fails.
  NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The short is **negative gross** at every horizon and worse net
  of a round-trip cost + short borrow (−0.157% to −0.837% across the 5–10 bps sweep).
  There is no edge to charge costs against.
- **"Crash incoming"? — BUSTED.** The evening star's claim to mark the top of an uptrend
  and predict a fall does not survive contact with 21.5 years of tape, once measured fairly
  against what the same basket does on an average day. Neither the strict gap nor the
  prior-uptrend filter saves it, and no individual name in the basket carries a
  Bonferroni-robust version of the story.
